abilityValue.description: A fixed racial modifier, or "any" if the player assigns it freely (see ability_modifiers.special for the amount).

special.description: Amount applied to each ability marked "any" (0 if none are "any").

value.description: Skill slug -- must match a `slug` in lookups/skills.json, e.g. culture, life_science.

id.description: Special-ability slug, e.g. lowlight_vision, darkvision. Open-ended (not in lookups/) -- racial special abilities aren't a closed set; grows as new races need one.

target.description: Optional situational tag, e.g. environmental_hazard, radiation.

value.description: Condition slug -- must match a `key` in lookups/conditions.json, e.g. sickened, flatFooted.

then.description: Catch-all passthrough of the app's own engine-wide Modifier shape (backend/src/mechanics-schema.js) -- covers everything the four sugar-typed variants above don't (energy resistance, AC, speed, initiative, attack/damage buckets, ...). Automated normalization (WebApp/starfinder-tool/backend/scripts/normalize-entries.js) emits this variant by passing a linked racial-feature's mechanics.modifiers[] through close to verbatim, so nothing is lossily remapped into the narrower vocabulary above.

modifierType_.description: SF1e bonus type, e.g. untyped/racial/circumstance/insight -- same-type bonuses from different sources don't stack except untyped/circumstance/dodge. Field literally named `type` on the wire (see modifier.type below), aliased here only to avoid clashing with bonusEffect's own `type` discriminator.

effectType.description: What this modifies, e.g. skill/save/ac/energy-resistance/all-attacks -- see Docs/04-data-pipeline-aon.md 'The Modifiers system'.

valueAffected.description: Narrows effectType further, e.g. which skill/save/energy type.

modifier.description: Formula string or constant, e.g. "5" or "@abilities.str.mod".

scope.description: What this note is about, e.g. a trait id, "alternate_traits[2].replaces", or "description_rulebook.names".

reason.description: Why this couldn't be confidently filled in automatically -- e.g. "replaces-sentence didn't match the expected pattern", "LLM classification below confidence threshold".

raw.description: The source text this was derived (or failed to be derived) from, so a human reviewer doesn't have to go dig it out of aon-cache again.

type.description: Creature type -- keep this enum in sync with lookups/creature_types.json (that file is the single source of truth; unverified against a rulebook, see its _provenance note).

subtype.description: Free text -- race lineage tag (e.g. "human", "vesk"), not a closed vocabulary like type.

condition_spec.description: e.g. the level number, when condition is "level".

traits.description: The race's default traits -- plural, since real races commonly grant several (e.g. Aasimar: Darkvision + Celestial Radiance + Celestial Resistance + Skilled, all at once, none of them optional). Was a single `trait` object in an earlier revision of this schema, which only fit races with exactly one default trait; corrected once real Foundry-sourced data (racial-features/*.json) showed that's not the common case.

source.description: Source book -- full title (e.g. "Alien Archive 2") matching aon-cache's own `source` field, or a short code from lookups/sourcebooks.json for hand-authored entries.
Source book -- full title matching aon-cache's own `source` field, or a short code from lookups/sourcebooks.json.
Source book -- full title matching aon-cache's own `source` field, or a short code from lookups/sourcebooks.json.

replaces.description: id of the trait (in `traits[]`, or another alternate_traits[].id) this one swaps out. null when a source's "This replaces X" sentence couldn't be resolved to a known trait id -- see _review.

_source.description: aon-cache slugs this entry was assembled from (the race entry itself plus every linked racial-feature) -- provenance for a reviewer who wants to go check the original scrape.

_review.description: Anything the normalization script (or its optional local-LLM assist) couldn't confidently fill in -- reviewed and cleared by a human before this entry is treated as final, rather than silently dropped or guessed. Empty/absent once fully reviewed.
